arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Ms. Karlan argued the Act sets two paths for district courts.
She stated restitution is a mandatory part of the sentence.
Mr. Heytens stated the government agrees no cases directly confront this issue.
He addressed the finality question raised by the Court.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: The Mandatory Victim Restitution Act requires courts to order restitution for certain crimes. It allows courts 90 days to set the final amount. The core conflict involves the timing of this order relative to the appeal window.

sections.heading: What each side wants
paragraphs: the side that brought the case wants to file an appeal immediately after sentencing.
The government wants to delay the appeal until the restitution order is final.

sections.heading: What each side says
paragraphs: the side that brought the case argues the 90-day period does not suspend the appeal deadline.
The government argues the sentence is not final until the restitution order is entered.

sections.heading: What the justices asked
paragraphs: Justice Alito asked if a 90-day delay prevents a defendant from appealing.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines when a criminal sentence becomes final. It determines if defendants must wait for restitution orders before appealing. It impacts the speed of criminal appeals nationwide.
